items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: Well, the first band I played with was with, I see Al Wynn, he had a little band at the Dreamland. ... Well, Al Wynn was one. I was one.

ctx.x: What happened when you got up to Chicago, Prince?

Well, I went in there with a big show from traveling on the road in the year of 1927. And the show was named the Miramak Miramakers. And after I got in Chicago, well, I struck all, struck luck there with fellas like Al Wynn, Tiny Palm, and Hughie Swift and all them kind of fellas. And I just got good there and made good. So I just stuck on, got to blowing around there. Got up together with a little fella called Francois Louisanans. He had been trying to get a band up together. So we worked together, say about…
Well, to get back to the, you're getting there, you were playing with Miramaks, Miramakas? Miramakas. Now who was the Bronze Bannikens? That was the same album?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: Yeah, Francois Mosley's band. Charlie Ducasse, myself, Fred Reed on piano... Al Wynn on trombone.

ctx.x: Oh, I wanted to ask you about Frankie Halfpaint Jackson. You made a record with him, huh? Oh, yeah. I made a record with him. You remember who was in that band?

Yeah, Francois Mosley's band. Charlie Ducasse, myself, Fred Reed on piano. And Charlie Ducasse on guitar and that boy, Lil Sax on tenor. Fred Howard on alto. He played alto on clarinet. And what else? Fred on piano, me on trumpet. Al Wynn on trombone. Al Wynn. I got a letter from him the other day. Little Sax's name is what? Robert Crowder. Everybody called him. You know who he was, Kenta? Y'all didn't know Cecil. He used to play with Earl Hein.

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: The only guy that made records was Tiny Pong, Al Wynn, Jimmy Wade.

ctx.x: Nice piano player. When you played with Jelly Roll did you ever make any records with him? No, I didn't.

He didn't make no while I was with him. He had made some before I got with him. But I don't think he made no more after that. Because he died right after I got out of the band, me and Swayze. He didn't live long. But I heard all his records, Dr. Jazz and all that kind of stuff. But I didn't make any with him. He never made any records? The only guy that made records was Tiny Pong, Al Wynn, Jimmy Wade. He was a big chief. And what this guy named in New York, uh, the trombones. He's an Indian. Big chief. Oh, you…
Yeah, Bunk was there that year too. The Bunk sure was.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: I would leave there and go into the Dreamland right across the street, see, and play there with them. ... Al when was doing the hiring, I know that, he hired me.

ctx.x: Well that was after Huey Swift? Yeah. And after Francois? Yeah.

Tiny Palm was after Francois? No, Tiny Palm was a little before Francois. See, I don't know if it, I don't know if it was Tiny Palm Band or Al when band, but they both was there together. See, you know, I think it was Tiny Palm, but Al when was doing a lot of managing, you know. But I'm pretty sure it was Tiny Palm Band, see.
Where at? At the Dreamland in Chicago. That's your first job on then?
